title: Cognitive Approach Adventure 1: Memory Models
welcome_lead: Today you'll compare the Multi-Store Model and the Working Memory Model.
meta_desc: Psychology Cognitive: Atkinson & Shiffrin's Multi-Store (1968) and Baddeley & Hitch Working Memory (1974).
final_note: You contrasted two memory architectures and their evidence.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Atkinson & Shiffrin (1968) saw memory as a flow.

Sensory store (Sperling 1960, iconic memory ~250 ms) → STM (~7 ± 2 items, Miller 1956) → LTM (rehearsal needed).

Support: HM kept STM but lost LTM. KF (Shallice & Warrington 1970) showed STM deficit but intact LTM — challenging the simple linear flow.

Baddeley & Hitch (1974) replaced STM with an active working memory.

Components: central executive, phonological loop (verbal), visuospatial sketchpad (visual), and (added 2000) the episodic buffer.

Evidence: dual-task experiments show two tasks using one component impair each other; two tasks across components don't.

MSM is intuitive but treats STM as a single passive store.

WMM explains how we can listen and read at once (different slaves) but not read two texts (same slave).

Both models complement each other — WMM zooms in on the box labelled 'STM'.
